clue.text: Correct account to a clergyman

parts.note: a curate is a clergyman, an assistant to a parish priest

explanation.surface: An instruction to send the right bill to the local vicar's assistant.
explanation.definitionFit: Something accurate is free from error, so the adjective swaps directly for correct.

clue.text: Rubbish dumps may offer their own rewards

explanation.surface: A wry thought that refuse heaps hand out their own prizes.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle words 'may offer their own' tie the two senses together: dumps of one kind offer gratuities of the other.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain a tip is a refuse dump; tips are also small cash rewards given for service.

clue.text: Comprehensive old girl holding tennis shot

indicators.note: one word holding another wraps around it, so the shot sits inside

parts.note: gal is an old-fashioned word for a girl
a lob is a high shot in tennis played over the opponent

explanation.surface: A former schoolgirl clutching a racket after a high return.
explanation.definitionFit: Global and comprehensive are synonyms meaning all-embracing or covering everything.

clue.text: Spy disguised: smart and clairvoyant

indicators.note: a disguised word has its letters rearranged so it is not recognised

parts.note: chic means smart or stylish

explanation.surface: An undercover agent who is well dressed and can also see the future.
explanation.definitionFit: A psychic claims supernatural perception, which is what a clairvoyant has.

clue.text: Negotiates pub profits

parts.note: a bar is a pub or drinking place
gains are profits

explanation.surface: A landlord haggling over the takings of the local.
explanation.definitionFit: To bargain is to negotiate terms, so the verbs agree in the third person.

clue.text: December speech calls for trimming

parts.note: an oration is a formal speech

explanation.surface: Christmas-season talk about putting up the tinsel.
explanation.definitionFit: A decoration is an ornament, and trimming is ornamentation added to something.

clue.text: Attitude of holy man, one attached to the Church

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for saint, a holy man
an is the indefinite article, meaning one
CE stands for the Church of England

explanation.surface: A saint's devotion to the Church described as his attitude.
explanation.definitionFit: A stance is a position or point of view, the same as an attitude.

clue.text: Greek hero caught cold in the turning tide

indicators.note: one piece is set in the middle of the other
the word is turned round so its letters run backwards

parts.note: the sea is the tidal water, standing for tide
a chill is the cold one catches

explanation.surface: A hero of legend falls ill while caught out by the changing tide.
explanation.walkthrough: 'caught cold' looks like two pieces but is one: to catch cold is to get a chill. 'turning' turns the tide word round.
explanation.definitionFit: Achilles is the great Greek warrior of the Trojan War in Homer's Iliad.

clue.text: Middlemen: one has knowledge that reaches backstreet

parts.note: a means one
gen is British slang for information or knowledge

indicators.note: the word back placed before street tells us to read its abbreviation backwards

explanation.surface: A go-between whose inside information extends to the back alleys.
explanation.walkthrough: The printed 'backstreet' is one word, but it splits: 'back' is the reversal signal for the street abbreviation that follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Agents act on behalf of others, the role of middlemen between parties.

clue.text: Turn to knock out addicts

indicators.note: to turn a word is to read it backwards

parts.note: to stun is to knock out

explanation.surface: Advice to a boxer to spin round and floor the opponent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn' reverses STUN to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Nuts is informal for enthusiasts or fanatics, people addicted to a hobby.

clue.text: History of old stadium

parts.note: back as an adjective means from the past, as in back numbers
a ground is a sports stadium

explanation.surface: The history of an ancient sports arena.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone's background is their past experience and history.

clue.text: Animal king seen in waterway

indicators.note: the king is seen in the middle of the waterway, a container signal

parts.note: a canal is an artificial waterway
R is the abbreviation for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A king of beasts spotted swimming along a canal.
explanation.definitionFit: Carnal means of the body or flesh, the animal side of human nature.

clue.text: Place for tots, males: many have green fingers

parts.note: a nursery is a place for small children
men are males

explanation.surface: Men at a playgroup turn out to be keen gardeners.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a descriptive phrase: these people, many of them, have green fingers. 'Green fingers' is the British idiom for gardening skill.
explanation.definitionFit: Nurserymen grow and sell plants, so as a trade they are people with a gift for gardening.

clue.text: Followed foolish one back round the art gallery

indicators.note: the reversed pair goes round the gallery, enclosing it
back tells us to read the pair of pieces in reverse order

parts.note: dim means stupid or foolish
I is the Roman numeral one
the Tate is the famous London art gallery

explanation.surface: A silly person trailing someone back around a museum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns the foolish one round as a unit, and 'round' wraps that result about the London gallery, splitting it before its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To imitate someone is to follow their example or copy them.

clue.text: Little boy breaks brush where Desdemona died

indicators.note: the boy breaks into the brush, splitting it open

parts.note: a broom is a brush for sweeping
Ed is a short name for a boy, here little as a pet name

explanation.surface: A small child smashing a broom handle.
explanation.walkthrough: In Shakespeare's Othello, Desdemona is smothered by her husband in her bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Desdemona is killed in her bedchamber, the room where she sleeps.

clue.text: One of Shakespeare's mistresses, all dried up

explanation.surface: A Shakespearean lady who has lost her bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: Mistress Overdone is the bawd in Measure for Measure.
explanation.definitionFit: Mistress Overdone is a Shakespeare character; food cooked too long is overdone and dried out.

clue.text: Endlessly hopeful for painkiller

indicators.note: endlessly means without its final letter, the end cut off

parts.note: aspiring means hopeful, wishing to achieve

explanation.surface: A forever optimistic sufferer reaching for relief.
explanation.definitionFit: Aspirin is a common drug taken to relieve pain.

clue.text: I'm not lacking fashions with time to be shameless

parts.note: taken as written, apostrophe dropped
modes are fashions or styles

explanation.surface: A boastful claim to have plenty of styles and time to show off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not lacking' simply links: I'M is kept whole and joined to the fashions.
explanation.definitionFit: Immodest means lacking modesty, bold and shameless in manner.

clue.text: Authorised to be blessed, but not initially

indicators.note: not initially means the first letter is dropped from the word

parts.note: hallowed means blessed or made holy

explanation.surface: Sanctioned to be holy, though only later.
explanation.definitionFit: Allowed means permitted, the same as authorised.

clue.text: Noble woman about to read pretty nearly — which is heavenly

indicators.note: the woman goes about the other piece, enclosing it

parts.note: the name Ethel comes from an Old English word meaning noble

indicators.note: pretty nearly means almost all, so the last letter goes

parts.note: taken as written before trimming

explanation.surface: An aristocratic lady about to read something nearly sublime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is a container signal here, not 're'; 'pretty nearly' drops the last letter of 'read'. The name Ethel derives from Old English for noble.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethereal means celestial or of the heavens, delicate and otherworldly.

clue.text: Gift requires thanks fast

parts.note: ta is British informal for thanks
Lent is the Christian season of fasting

explanation.surface: A present that calls for gratitude and abstinence.
explanation.definitionFit: A talent is a natural ability, what we call a gift.

clue.text: Came in confused by moving pictures

indicators.note: confused letters are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone who wandered in bewildered by the films.
explanation.definitionFit: The cinema is the medium of films, which are moving pictures.

clue.text: Name half hidden in communication that's false

indicators.note: the half name is concealed inside the communication

parts.note: a card is a written message or communication

indicators.note: half takes the first two of the four letters

explanation.surface: Half a name tucked into a deceptive message.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half' takes the front half of 'Name', and 'hidden in' tucks it into the communication.
explanation.definitionFit: A canard is a false rumour or report, something untrue put about.

clue.text: Acted with fine feathers, but pooh-poohed as unimportant

parts.note: played means acted a part
down is the fine soft feathers of a bird

explanation.surface: A performer in plumes whose show was dismissed.
explanation.definitionFit: To play something down is to minimise it, treating it as unimportant.

clue.text: Old bird going from one party to another

parts.note: a do is a party
another party, so another do

explanation.surface: An ageing socialite moving between gatherings.
explanation.walkthrough: The dodo is a flightless bird, extinct since the seventeenth century.
explanation.definitionFit: The dodo is an extinct bird, so it is fairly called old.

clue.text: Just a little water for a doctor turned good

indicators.note: turned means read backwards

parts.note: pi is short for pious, meaning good

explanation.surface: A doctor gone virtuous offering only a sip.
explanation.definitionFit: A drip is a single falling drop of liquid, just a little water.

clue.text: Put away in a Pinter narrative

indicators.note: in tells us the letters sit inside the run of words

explanation.surface: Something stowed in a story by the playwright Harold Pinter.
explanation.definitionFit: To intern is to confine or imprison, which is to put someone away.

clue.text: First nobleman to have broken ties

parts.note: an earl is a British nobleman

indicators.note: broken letters are scattered and put back together differently

explanation.surface: An aristocrat who leads by snapping his bonds.
explanation.definitionFit: Earliest means the first in time.
